instruction: Go to the NBA schedule page on nba.com.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter 'active_url_from_accessTree' correctly extracts the active Chrome tab URL from the accessibility tree, which is the right state to verify navigation tasks.
Metric 'is_expected_url_pattern_match' correctly handles the 'type: rule' parameter convention — it accesses rules['expected'] directly (not rules.get('rules', ...)), which is correct.
The regex pattern 'nba\\.com.*schedule' correctly matches valid NBA schedule URLs such as 'https://www.nba.com/schedule', and requires both 'nba.com' and 'schedule' to appear in the URL.
Initial state (nba.com homepage) does not contain 'schedule' in the URL, so the evaluator provides negative-control resistance — the task cannot be trivially passed without navigation.
The task has a single, simple requirement (navigate to the schedule page) which is fully covered by a single URL pattern check. No multi-step coverage gaps.
